name: browser-use
headline: ai writing guide with specialized agents
short_description: AI writing guide automates software development workflows. It uses 94 specialized agents and 65+ commands for multi-agent coordination. Reduces manual oversight and extends runtime. Integrates with Claude Code, Warp, and Factory AI.
author: jmagly

sections.overview:
AIWG is a deployment framework that synchronizes AI agents, skills, commands, and rules across 10 platforms—Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Warp, and six others—from one source of truth. It ships 200+ pre-built agents, 67+ CLI commands, and 400+ deployable artifacts organized into 8 core frameworks covering SDLC workflows, digital forensics, research management, marketing operations, media curation, infrastructure, and knowledge base tasks. Users install globally via npm, then deploy specialized agent teams (like a 180-agent SDLC auditor) with a single command. The framework handles artifact memory, background orchestration, autonomous loops, and cost telemetry—reducing manual coordination across multi-platform AI workflows.
Deploy specialized security and compliance review agents across all development tools
Automate SDLC workflows with parallel agent teams for architecture, testing, and code review
Manage research and knowledge base curation with dedicated agent frameworks
Synchronize marketing operations and media curation agents across team environments
Built a scalable e-commerce backend using Node.js, Express, and MongoDB with a microservices architecture. The system includes:
- User Service (Authentication, Profiles)
- Product Service (Inventory, Catalog)
- Order Service (Checkout, Payments)
- API Gateway (Rate Limiting, Request Routing)
sections.setup:
No install command available. Check the GitHub repository for manual installation instructions.
`git clone https://github.com/jmagly/ai-writing-guide`
1. Clone repository: `git clone https://github.com/yourorg/ecommerce-microservices.git`
2. Install dependencies: `npm install` (root) and `npm install` (each service)
3. Start services: `docker-compose up -d`
4. Run migrations: `npm run migrate:up`
5. Seed data: `npm run seed:dev`
